[F13 F14 F15 F16 F17] [NS-1 NS-2]
C8: Because the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him 613 m from the pickup point (far outside the 200 m arrival radius), this is the abuse-of-arrival-button case that additionally warrants account review (F5). [F5] [NS-2]
C9: The driver's history of two upheld no-show disputes in 90 days supports sending this case to account review as a repeat pattern (F19). [F19] [RD-6]

claims.assertion: The trip was cancelled by the driver at 08:19:30 after the driver had tapped 'I'm Here' at 08:16:00, so the case is screened under NS-1/NS-2 (driver-side no-show cancellation) rather than a rider cancellation.

NS-1(ii) fails: at the moment of the 'I'm Here' tap the GPS puts the driver 613 m from the pickup point (closest approach 612 m at 08:15:30, never within 200 m), so the driver was not at the pick-up location according to GPS data.

NS-1(iii) also fails: after the tap the driver spent 0 s within 200 m of the pickup point, and no platform arrival record exists (driver_arrived_at is null), so there is no continuous >3-minute wait at the pickup point.

The driver's written explanation ('Victoria Street was jammed solid, I could not get any closer') is contradicted by the traffic record: Victoria Street was recorded at speed band 3 (20–29 km/h), not severe congestion, and no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window, with fair weather.

The driver's 08:16 message 'I'm here already, please come out' and the 08:19 message 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling' are not supported by any GPS record placing the car at the Victoria St entrance, so they cannot establish the NS-1 elements.

The rider did everything asked of her: she messaged at 08:14 that she was waiting at the Victoria St entrance and at 08:17 asked for the plate because no car was visible — consistent with a car that was 613 m away.
The $6.61 cancellation fee on record (F6) therefore fails its NS-1 preconditions and must be refunded in full; the rider's own profile shows no dispute history and a 4.9 rating.

Because the driver tapped 'I'm Here' while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius, NS-2's second limb applies and the account action of the 'Abuse of the cancellation and waiting time button' type is triggered by the record itself; the same record shows the flaw is a repeated pattern (2 of 2 prior no-show disputes upheld in 90 days), so an account review is properly attached.

weaknesses: The driver's non-arrival is fully documented (F1, F2, F5): 613 m away, 0 s inside 200 m after the tap, and no platform arrival record (F4) — this is the rider's strongest material and I cannot contest it.

To resist the refund I would have to rely on the driver's written statement (F13) that Victoria Street was impassable, but the traffic facts (F14 band 3, F16 no incidents) contradict it, and the policy prefers system records; so no RD-4 'reasonable cause' excuse is available.
The driver's own chat messages (F9, F11) assert an arrival and a compliance wait that the GPS facts do not support, which reads badly and pushes the case toward a fraud-type account flag.
The driver's 90-day record shows 2 no-show disputes already upheld (F19), which under RD-6 converts this case into a 'repeated' pattern and makes a bare no_action outcome unrealistic.
The refund must be issued as a Ryde voucher rather than cash and is only a recommendation, per NS-7, so I cannot promise the rider a cash refund.

NS-1(ii) fails on the records. At the moment of the arrival tap the driver's GPS position was 613 m from the pickup point, and his closest approach all trip was 612 m — he never entered the 200 m arrival radius [F5][F1]. The screen's own check marks this element ✗.

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee only stands if the driver pressed "I'm Here" while actually at the pickup point; GPS shows his closest approach to pickup was 612 m at 08:15:30 and he never came within 200 m (F1, F2).
The arrival tap itself fails the location test: at 08:16:00, when the driver tapped "I'm Here", he was 613 m from the pickup point, and he stayed within 200 m for 0 seconds after the tap (F5).
The continuous-wait requirement is also unmet: the driver was stationary only at a point 613 m away from 08:13:10 to 08:19:30, so no waiting inside the pickup area ever occurred (F2, F5).
The platform's own timeline never placed the driver at the pickup point — driver_arrived_at is null — which corroborates the GPS record rather than the driver's statement (F4, F1).

The rider was at the named meeting point and actively tried to be found: at 08:14 she wrote she was waiting at the Victoria St entrance, at 08:17 she said she saw no car and asked for the plate, and the driver never gave it (F8, F10).

The driver's chat claim "I'm here already, please come out" (08:16) is contradicted by the system records showing him 613 m away at that moment, and under the system-records-priority rule his untruthful arrival claim cannot support the fee (F9, F5, F4).

The driver's excuse that "Victoria Street was jammed solid" does not save the fee: the only traffic records show Victoria Street and North Bridge Road at speed band 3 (20–29 km/h), no congestion band and no incident near the route, and weather fair with 0.0 mm rain (F13, F14, F15, F16, F17).

Because the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him 613 m from the pickup point (far outside the 200 m arrival radius), this is the abuse-of-arrival-button case that additionally warrants account review (F5).
The driver's history of two upheld no-show disputes in 90 days supports sending this case to account review as a repeat pattern (F19).
The rider has no disputes in 90 days and a 4.9 rating, so the fee is not a pattern of rider misuse (F18).

The disputed $6.61 cancellation fee is a recorded charge on this trip, so full refund of that amount is computable from the fare fact (F6), and the refund follows Ryde's voucher route for cancellation-fee disputes (F3, F6).

weaknesses: The driver did tap "I'm Here" (F5) and did wait over 3 minutes before cancelling (F2: stationary 6 min 20 s; F3: cancelled 9 min 25 s after acceptance), so the only thing defeating the fee is the 200 m location requirement, not any lack of patience.

The driver's written statement that he could not get closer because Victoria Street was jammed (F13) is chronologically consistent with him being stationary 613 m away (F2); the counter is only that the recorded traffic level (band 3, 20–29 km/h) and the absence of any incident (F14, F15, F16) do not amount to a severe blockage.

The traffic facts F14/F15 cover Victoria Street and North Bridge Road generally, not the specific 613 m stretch between the driver's stationary point and the Victoria St entrance, so the judge may find the road near the pickup was slower than the band suggests.
There is no GPS evidence of where the rider physically stood (F8, F10 are her own messages), so her presence at the entrance rests on the chat record rather than a system location fact.

claims.assertion: The trip was cancelled by the driver at 08:19:30 after the driver had tapped 'I'm Here' at 08:16:00, so the case is screened under NS-1/NS-2 (driver-side no-show cancellation) rather than a rider cancellation.

NS-1(ii) fails: at the moment of the 'I'm Here' tap the GPS puts the driver 613 m from the pickup point (closest approach 612 m at 08:15:30, never within 200 m), so the driver was not at the pick-up location according to GPS data.

NS-1(iii) also fails: after the tap the driver spent 0 s within 200 m of the pickup point, and no platform arrival record exists (driver_arrived_at is null), so there is no continuous >3-minute wait at the pickup point.

The driver's written explanation ('Victoria Street was jammed solid, I could not get any closer') is contradicted by the traffic record: Victoria Street was recorded at speed band 3 (20–29 km/h), not severe congestion, and no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window, with fair weather.

The driver's 08:16 message 'I'm here already, please come out' and the 08:19 message 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling' are not supported by any GPS record placing the car at the Victoria St entrance, so they cannot establish the NS-1 elements.

The rider did everything asked of her: she messaged at 08:14 that she was waiting at the Victoria St entrance and at 08:17 asked for the plate because no car was visible — consistent with a car that was 613 m away.
The $6.61 cancellation fee on record (F6) therefore fails its NS-1 preconditions and must be refunded in full; the rider's own profile shows no dispute history and a 4.9 rating.

Because the driver tapped 'I'm Here' while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius, NS-2's second limb applies and the account action of the 'Abuse of the cancellation and waiting time button' type is triggered by the record itself; the same record shows the flaw is a repeated pattern (2 of 2 prior no-show disputes upheld in 90 days), so an account review is properly attached.

weaknesses: The driver's non-arrival is fully documented (F1, F2, F5): 613 m away, 0 s inside 200 m after the tap, and no platform arrival record (F4) — this is the rider's strongest material and I cannot contest it.

To resist the refund I would have to rely on the driver's written statement (F13) that Victoria Street was impassable, but the traffic facts (F14 band 3, F16 no incidents) contradict it, and the policy prefers system records; so no RD-4 'reasonable cause' excuse is available.

Conceded — the tap at 613 m from the pickup point is the recorded abuse-of-arrival-button situation under NS-2's second limb; the account review is for Ryde, not a fee question.
